tasks.short: Prepare compulsory evidence requests through legal counsel and track authorised service.

steps.what: Gather the allegation, evidence gaps and proposed recipients.

loop.input: Case documents, evidence register and request template.
loop.output: Evidence request brief with source references and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Investigator checks every requested item, recipient and source reference.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing sources return to the investigator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text allegations require interpretation; fixed fields cannot identify all evidence gaps.

steps.what: Assess lawful routes, necessity, scope and restrictions under national rules.
Prepare the application and supporting exhibit bundle.
Check and submit the application through the applicable legal channel.
Decide whether to issue a compulsory evidence order.
Serve an issued order using the authorised method.
Record service, response deadlines and follow-up responsibilities.

tasks.design: A restricted case register in {WORKFLOW} links evidence in {DOCS}; a bounded drafting loop prepares the request brief, while deterministic templates assemble approved applications and exhibits. Legal counsel controls submission, competent authorities control issuance, and authorised officers control service under national rules. Confirmed service details create deadlines in {CALENDAR} and reminders through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Legal procedures vary, supporting evidence is scattered, and corporate investigators usually lack compulsory powers. Templates help, but they do not resolve legal authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records and workflow tools support restricted access, templates and reminders. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort; a bounded loop can prepare source-linked briefs for review.
tasks.still_hard: Jurisdiction, privilege, lawful scope, service validity and restricted evidence access require specialist judgement. GDPR applies, including restrictions on criminal-offence data; EU AI Act obligations depend on the actual use.
tasks.human_edge: The investigator explains why evidence matters. Legal counsel judges necessity, proportionality and the lawful route.

ambition.what: Evidence request readiness checks for legal counsel

tasks.altitude: The investigator spends less time assembling bundles and chasing deadlines, and more time testing evidence gaps. They can prioritise readiness checks but gain no power to compel disclosure or serve orders.

reach.task: Review evidence access and retention controls.
reach.learn: Lawful purpose, criminal-offence data restrictions, retention and access logging.
Source references, reconciliation and evidence provenance.

evidence.claim: Corporate investigators generally coordinate compulsory evidence requests through legally authorised channels; procedures depend on national rules.
DataSnipper supports evidence extraction and testing with human review; this supports bundle preparation, not legal issuance or service.
Baker Tilly Netherlands reported evidence-checking time savings with DataSnipper; these vendor-reported results do not establish subpoena savings.
Unlawful fraud records can cause serious harm; the Dutch fraud-list case illustrates the need for lawful scope and access controls.

assumptions: This supplemental occupation task is uncommon in a mid-size company. The normal corporate role prepares and coordinates requests.
Shares are indicative active effort across the represented participants, including external roles; they exclude waiting for decisions or service.
The in-person service step represents one possible national procedure, not a universal requirement.
The prior's high gathering and coordination shares are plausible, but do not establish corporate legal authority.
Build estimates cover one jurisdiction and one request route, excluding authority processing time.
Consent and access estimates include privacy review and any applicable employee consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which national procedures and legal powers apply?
Who may apply, submit and serve in the organisation's actual cases?
What restricted case storage and approved templates already exist?
Which authority channels accept electronic submissions or status data?
Does the proposed processing require employee consultation or a data protection impact assessment?
research_questions: Which request fields and exhibits can be generated from approved structured data?
Can service details be received as structured records rather than manually transcribed?
What validation demonstrates correct deadlines, exhibit references and access restrictions?
new_work: Review source-linked briefs and resolve missing evidence.
Maintain national procedure templates and deadline rules.
Check access logs and retention schedules.
Handle rejected applications and disputed service records.

tasks.short: Refer substantiated fraud concerns to authorities and support any lawful arrest by authorised officers.

steps.what: Assemble the evidence chronology, identity records and unresolved contradictions.

loop.input: Approved case documents, transaction records and evidence register.
loop.output: Chronology with source references, contradictions and missing information.
loop.check: Investigator verifies identities, dates and references; amounts reconcile deterministically to source records.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved contradictions remain explicit for human investigation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative evidence requires reading and synthesis; a template alone cannot expose conflicting accounts.

steps.what: Assess disclosure grounds and approve the referral's scope.
Submit the referral and answer factual questions from authorities.
Determine whether legal grounds and required authority for arrest exist.
Carry out any lawful arrest and required immediate safeguards.
Record any authorised status update in the company case file.

tasks.design: A restricted register in {WORKFLOW} links evidence in {DOCS} and reconciled transaction records from {ERP}. A bounded loop drafts a source-linked chronology for investigator review, and configured forms record approved referrals and permitted status updates. Legal referral decisions and all arrest decisions and actions remain with authorised people under national rules.
tasks.previous_blocker: Arrest is an exercise of public authority, usually outside a corporate investigator's role. Evidence preparation is also fragmented and requires careful distinction between allegation and fact.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured evidence registers and source-linked drafting can reduce dossier preparation. No technical development changes the investigator's legal powers or makes physical arrest suitable for automation.
tasks.still_hard: Credibility, identity, conflicting evidence and lawful disclosure require judgement. GDPR restrictions on criminal-offence data apply; EU AI Act classification must follow the actual use, especially if a system is proposed for law enforcement.
tasks.human_edge: Investigators test alternative explanations and give accurate evidence. Authorised officers assess legal grounds, immediate circumstances and safeguards.
tasks.altitude: The corporate investigator has somewhat more time for corroboration and factual support to authorities. Arrest powers and decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare a lawful disclosure assessment for a criminal referral.
reach.learn: Purpose limitation, disclosure grounds and restrictions on criminal-offence data.

reach.task: Reconcile the financial loss schedule supporting a referral.
reach.learn: Separate confirmed loss, disputed amounts and estimates with traceable workpapers.

evidence.claim: Corporate fraud investigators normally support authorities rather than exercise police arrest powers; exact powers depend on national rules.
Source-linked evidence compilation and human review are feasible preparation patterns; this is not evidence of automated arrest capability.
The Dutch fraud-list case documents harm from unlawful fraud-related records and supports careful limits on dossier processing.
Sensitive referral preparation can use bounded drafting, but arrest judgement and physical action remain human responsibilities.

assumptions: The company investigator has no special arrest powers.
Steps describe a conditional cross-organisation path ending in arrest only if authorities independently establish grounds.
Shares estimate active effort across the represented participants; they exclude waiting and do not describe the corporate investigator's personal timesheet.
The competent authority may be an authorised officer or judicial authority, depending on national rules.
The prior's workflow-automation preference applies mainly to preparation. Its interface estimates do not justify automation of arrest.
Build estimates cover corporate referral support, excluding police systems and operational procedures.
Consent and access estimates include privacy review and applicable consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Does this task occur at all within the company's investigator role?
Which authority receives referrals and what submission format does it require?
What disclosure grounds, restrictions and retention periods apply?
What status information may authorities share back?
Are any employee-monitoring data included, and what consultation is required?
research_questions: Which dossier sections can use fixed templates without narrative generation?
How should reviewers verify that summaries preserve contradictions and exculpatory evidence?
What minimum dataset is sufficient for each approved referral route?
new_work: Verify chronology drafts against source evidence.
Check that contrary evidence and uncertainty remain visible.
Maintain referral templates and disclosure permissions.
Audit dossier access and remove records when retention expires.

tasks.short: Negotiate recovery of fraud losses and document, approve and monitor agreed repayments.

steps.what: Reconcile supported losses, prior recoveries and disputed amounts.
Approve recovery objectives, concession limits and escalation conditions.
Prepare repayment options and a source-linked negotiation brief.

loop.input: Approved mandate, reconciled loss schedule and relevant correspondence.
loop.output: Negotiation brief explaining deterministically calculated repayment options and disputed points.
loop.check: Code checks amounts and mandate limits; investigator checks source references, tone and disputed facts.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported facts or out-of-mandate proposals return to the investigator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations use code, but correspondence and contested explanations require reading and concise drafting.

steps.what: Discuss responsibility, practical repayment capacity and proposed terms with the responsible party.
Prepare and review settlement wording, releases and default provisions.
Approve the final settlement and release it for signature.
Execute the agreement through authorised signatures.
Register repayment dates, match receipts and flag missed payments.

tasks.design: A restricted recovery register in {WORKFLOW} reconciles approved losses and receipts from {ERP} and {BANK}, calculates repayment options, and feeds a bounded briefing loop using evidence in {DOCS}. People negotiate and approve terms; deterministic templates prepare settlement documents in {CLM}, with signature routing through {ESIGN}. Signed structured terms create repayment schedules in {ERP}, while payment exceptions return to the investigator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Negotiations resist fixed rules, so preparation and follow-up often remain attached to manual casework. Loss calculations, correspondence and settlement terms also sit in separate records.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic calculations, document templates and signature workflows already exist. AI-assisted coding makes the connections cheaper to build, while bounded drafting reduces briefing effort without replacing negotiation.
tasks.still_hard: Responsibility may be disputed, repayment capacity uncertain and concessions commercially sensitive. Enforceability, employment deductions and settlement restrictions depend on national rules; GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties still apply.
tasks.human_edge: The investigator listens, tests credibility and negotiates workable terms. Legal counsel protects enforceability, and finance managers accept concessions within delegated authority.

ambition.what: Weekly recovery strategy decisions for stalled repayment plans

tasks.altitude: The investigator spends less time rebuilding loss schedules and chasing receipts, and more time preparing difficult negotiations. They can recommend revised terms weekly; binding concessions remain within the approved mandate and signature authority.

reach.task: Handle missed settlement instalments and propose a revised collection approach.
reach.learn: Payment allocation, arrears conversations and escalation thresholds.

reach.task: Compare recovery scenarios and expected shortfalls.
reach.learn: Scenario assumptions, uncertainty and the distinction between expected recovery and recognised income.

evidence.claim: Repayment arithmetic, receipt matching, template generation and reminders can use deterministic technology; negotiations remain human.
Moody's Credit Memo drafts financial narratives from documents and templates; this is adjacent evidence for briefing, not evidence of automated settlement negotiation.
The spreadsheet benchmark in the digest reports material calculation errors, supporting deterministic arithmetic and source tie-outs.
Dutch rules require works council consent for certain employee-monitoring arrangements; consultation requirements elsewhere depend on national rules.

assumptions: Negotiation is a conditional recovery process, not a finding that every accused person is responsible.
Shares estimate active case effort across participating roles and exclude waiting for replies, signatures or instalments.
The prior's high communication share fits negotiation; preparation and payment administration remain open to automation.
Existing settlement templates and delegated financial limits can be encoded after legal approval.
Automatic payment matching uses unique references or exact rules; ambiguous receipts become exceptions.
Build estimates cover one recovery process and existing finance and signature interfaces.
Consent and access estimates include privacy review and applicable employee consultation; no new employee-monitoring analytics are assumed.
unknowns: Who approves concessions, write-offs and settlement signatures?
Are cases employee, supplier, customer or third-party recoveries?
Which loss components are disputed, insured or already recovered?
Are structured settlement terms available for repayment scheduling?
Do existing systems expose reliable transaction identifiers and receipt feeds?
What employee consultation and restrictions apply to the underlying evidence?
research_questions: Which repayment calculations and matching rules cover the common cases?
Which settlement clauses can be populated safely from an approved template?
How will the system distinguish a missed payment from an unmatched receipt?
What evidence shows that a briefing draft preserves disputes and stays within the mandate?
new_work: Review loss schedules and briefing drafts.
Resolve ambiguous receipts and disputed loss components.
Handle payment exceptions and renegotiation requests.
Maintain templates, delegated limits and integration mappings.
Monitor access, retention and the accuracy of recovery status.

role.altitude: The investigator becomes better prepared for legal requests, authority referrals and recovery negotiations. They gain clearer case priorities and faster financial evidence, while coercive powers, legal approvals and binding settlement authority remain with the authorised roles.
reach: Accountants and auditors: reconcile losses and maintain traceable evidence.
Compliance officers: assess lawful disclosure, access and retention.
Bill and account collectors: manage repayment exceptions and recovery conversations.
Financial risk specialists: compare uncertain recovery scenarios.
skills_to_grow: Lawful handling of criminal-offence and employee data
Negotiation and assessment of conflicting accounts
role.ambitious_version: Run a shared evidence-readiness and recovery-support service for smaller business units, giving legal counsel traceable referrals and finance managers current recovery options without expanding investigative powers.
